text:
Travis Sanheim plays 25 minutes a night for a Flyers team that keeps losing the chance battle, and he has one goal in 18 games. He hasn't scored in 16 straight on 3.0 expected goals. Those chances usually turn into goals; he's shooting 2.9% against a normal range of 5% to 9% for a defenseman.

The larger story is the team around him. Philadelphia takes 45% of the expected goals with Sanheim on the ice at five on five, which sounds bad until you see that the Flyers are almost six points worse without him. He's the defenseman holding the dam. Evolving-Hockey had him 23rd among 215 defensemen last season at 2.3 wins above replacement, with competition in the 92nd percentile and a strong defensive impact.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds the fun part: he gets to the home-plate area in front of the net at an 86th percentile rate and does a third of his shooting off the rush. His top shot ranks in the 93rd percentile. We project about 36 points. On a team projected for 75 points, he is one of the reasons it isn't worse.
headline: Sanheim's goal drought won't last
